text:
sam: Observed apiserver 502/503 spike in eu-central starting 2024-05-07T12:10:00Z, coincident with a GPU onboarding burst. Controller-manager liveness probes started failing.
anya: Alerts: apiserver 5xx rate peaked at 6% for ~5m. kube-proxy on new nodes shows large number of outbound connections to apiserver (SYN_RECV).
matt: Looks like ephemeral port / SNAT exhaustion on the NATs. conntrack went from 30k->140k in 90s, cloud limit is 150k. Some NATs hit soft-fail and started dropping packets.
sam: Etcd metrics: wal_sync_duration_seconds p50 jumped to 300ms during same window, and leader disk iops spiked. Could be compaction or snapshot writeback.
anya: apiserver logs include repeated `EOF` and `clientv3: etcdserver: request timed out` around leader election. Example: ```E0512 12:11:22.789 auth.go:307] clientv3: grpc: the connection is unavailable```
matt: Controller-manager restarted twice; system OOMs seen on ctrlmgr process while reconciling thousands of new pods. Memory use jumped because informers tried to list all pods across the new node set.
infra-bot: Note: scale event initiated by gpu-autoscaler (policy=batch) at 12:09:58 UTC, +60 nodes attached by 12:11:30 UTC.
sam: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) pause autoscaler attach jobs, 2) reduce kube-proxy churn by setting `probeInitialDelaySeconds` longer temporarily, 3) increase conntrack limit on NATs, 4) divert non-critical model reads to eu-west.
anya: I'll patch autoscaler to slow bursts: `kubectl -n infra patch deploy/gpu-autoscaler --type merge -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"RollingUpdate","rollingUpdate":{"maxUnavailable":50}}}}'` (temp). Also adding a 30s random jitter to the attach loop.
matt: Running `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=220000` on NATs now and asking cloud to raise SNAT pool size. Ticket opened: CLOUD-9812.
sam: Also decided to mark new nodes as `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=true` until we have control-plane stability so pod churn is limited.
anya: Quick check: after throttling, conntrack fell to 80k in 6m, apiserver 5xxs down to ~1.2%. Controller-manager restarts stopped.
k8s-bot: Observed: etcd leader compaction started at 12:10:50 UTC, compactor held io for ~45s, follower replication lag increased.
matt: For postmortem items: - autoscaler burst policy lacks soft-splay - etcd compaction/snapshot timing collided with onboard - NAT conntrack headroom insufficient for sudden fanout - controller-manager memory request marginal for large reconciles.
sam: Long-term fixes agreed: 1) add autoscaler smoothing and jitter, 2) gate attach concurrency by control-plane health signals, 3) move compaction jobs to low-traffic windows + add rate limit, 4) increase controller-manager memory limits and tune informer resync cadence, 5) evaluate per-node SNAT or EIP pools for heavy fleet attach workloads.
anya: I'll draft config PRs and runbook updates. Suggest we add an alert: `apiserver_5xx > 2% AND conntrack_utilization > 70% => autoscaler throttle` so this can auto-mitigate next time.
matt: Cost note: per-region SNAT increase and larger NAT appliances add cost. Prefer autoscaler smoother as primary control, NAT increases as secondary.
sam: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open until logs are in the archive and ticket CLOUD-9812 is resolved. Will write up a short postmortem once we have metrics aligned. :white_check_mark:
